findings.title: Daylight, Zenith, and Celestial Marking
findings.claim: Favor's specifically named lunar station can, beside sky, daylight, zenith, and distinguishing marks in the preceding context, picture the route through recognizable positions within a larger order.
findings.mechanism: The name word's overhead-sky image provides the setting for the lunar station associated with na'amah, while yawm supplies daylight and mustaqim's noon image supplies a sun-position marker. The distinguishing mark in al-alamin makes these positions usable for orientation, returning the image to the favored road.
findings.reader_payoff: A favored trajectory acquires the analogy of a locatable station rather than an unmeasured stretch of motion.
findings.containment: The lunar station is an attested transferred name associated with ostrich resemblance, not a generic 'station' meaning of an'amta. No travel time, astronomy doctrine, or particular calendar date is inferred; daylight and lunar marking can supply different coordinates. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: Rivalry, Resistance, and Repeated War
findings.claim: The wrath-root's opposition image can make the excluded relation look like resistance grown into sustained conflict, against the earlier petition for an upright course.
findings.mechanism: Opposition associated with maghdub meets mustaqim's facing-off and undertaking images; the help root's seasoned war supplies repetition, the name root's rivalry supplies competitive pressure, and hamd's praised champion supplies reputation at stake. These roles describe escalation from comparison through resolve to reciprocal force.
findings.reader_payoff: The negative boundary can be heard as a damaged relation maintained by repeated resistance.
findings.containment: The passive maghdub still names those receiving wrath, not an active fighting verb. Reciprocal opposition is a root-family analogy, not proof of the recipients' motives, a narrated war, or a divine rivalry. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: The Marked and Straight Route

findings.mechanism: Sirat's road in 1:7 repeats 1:6 and brings the latter's guidance and straightness into contact with al-alamin's route marks. The worship root supplies a trodden, smoothed road, malik a road's middle course, and din a habitual way; together route perception and repeated practice explain how a road can also be a manner of life.

findings.containment: The prepared-road and middle-course images remain contextual resonances; worship remains worship, malik remains the sovereign addressee, and worlds are not lexically replaced by signposts. findings.title: Upright Stature and Balanced Strength

findings.mechanism: The Day word's open duration meets increase in an'amta; hamd's praiseworthy utmost gives an end, the worship root's brief delay and quick run supply differing rates, and guidance-root composure with rabb's staying supplies continuity. Progress is thus related to an end and a manner, rather than measured by speed alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The prayer's favored trajectory can include persistent, composed intensification.
findings.containment: The praiseworthy utmost and rates remain their idiomatic source images. No chronology of the recipients or guarantee of endless quantitative increase is supplied. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: Hunt, Flight, and Scattered Routes
findings.claim: The final loss can take the spatial shape of a group dispersed under pursuit, making the contrast with a shared favored road one of broken relational placement.
findings.mechanism: Hunters setting out in the name root provide pursuit; scattered groups and routes in the worship root provide divergent directions; mustaqim's community supplies the group that can disperse. The favor root's bird-idiom of flight, departure, and lost cohesion meets dallin's loss-from-a-holder relation, making separation consequential.
findings.reader_payoff: The danger concerns the integrity of a shared course and the difficulty of recovering those dispersed.
findings.containment: The bird idiom is cited as a construction-bound analogy activated by independent pursuit and scattered-route images, not as a lexical sense of the benefaction verb or of a bare bird name. No actual hunt or flight is asserted. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: Lesion, Swelling, and Localized Pain
findings.claim: The eye-region swelling associated with the wrath root can, in the context's bodily-pain images, make a damaged route relation felt as localized affliction as well as externally marked distress.
findings.mechanism: The eye-root-family image here belongs to maghdub: an upper-lid protrusion and associated swelling. Mustaqim's pain lodged in an organ provides felt distress, al-alamin's cleft lip supplies a different visible lesion, and the mercy root's postpartum womb ailment adds internal pain following birth. External marking and internal suffering become distinguishable aspects of the analogy.
findings.reader_payoff: A visible sign of distress need not exhaust what the affected person suffers.
findings.containment: These are distinct bodily images, not a diagnosis, a claim that a congenital protrusion is painful, or an account of divine anatomy. Postpartum specificity is retained only for its source image; impairment does not imply moral blame. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

epistemic.reason: The source descriptors and contextual carriers are supplied; the transfer between them and the focus is an interpretive analogy with the primary meanings preserved.

findings.title: Patronage, Support, and Claimed Recognition
findings.claim: The acknowledgment of favor can expose the relation between support and recognition: the preceding praise and aid vocabulary makes dependence on benefaction audible, alongside the human possibility of claiming credit for it.
findings.mechanism: An'amta's delivered benefit meets requested help, malik's mainstay, mustaqim's livelihood support, and rabb's conferred good. Hamd's claim-to-praise image then connects sustaining another person with seeking acknowledgment of that support.
findings.reader_payoff: Recognition of a benefactor becomes relationally concrete, with the burden that human patronage can attach to aid kept visible.
findings.containment: Claiming credit is a human relational analogy, not an assertion that God boasts, coerces praise, or conditions every favor on repayment. The primary prayer itself acknowledges the giver. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

epistemic.reason: The source descriptors and contextual carriers are supplied; the transfer between them and the focus is an interpretive analogy with the primary meanings preserved.

findings.title: Replacement, Indemnity, and Redress
findings.claim: The exception root can picture redress as a substitute answer to loss, with the preceding judgment and ownership vocabulary giving the replacement an accountable setting.
findings.mechanism: Dallin's lost possession and unavenged blood meet ghayr's indemnity and replacement images. Mustaqim's standing in another's place makes substitution concrete; malik's transfer of ownership and din's recompense connect the substitute with a settled claim.
findings.reader_payoff: Exclusion can acquire the analogy of a harmful outcome answered by another available course.
findings.containment: Ghayr remains the grammatical exclusion. No indemnity is asserted to have been paid in this ayah and no general law or redemption transaction follows from the analogy. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: Water-Secured Encampment and Livelihood
findings.claim: Ghayr's irrigation image can make the requested favored road depend on provision reaching a livable place: water gathered and controlled becomes sustenance distributed to land and people.
findings.mechanism: The rain-watering facet associated with ghayr meets rabb's abundant collected water and al-alamin's water-rich well. Malik's water as control of a camp links possession of the resource to settlement, and mustaqim's subsistence image supplies the life maintained by its delivery.
findings.reader_payoff: The road's well-being becomes a concrete dependency on sustained provision and its distribution.
findings.containment: The branch's ordinary provisioning core accompanies its rain-watering specialization. No actual irrigation command is translated from ghayr and no water infrastructure is asserted as a historical fact. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

findings.title: Engulfing and Penetrating Passage
findings.claim: The repeated road's swallowing and cutting imagery can distinguish passage that takes something through a medium from disappearance that leaves it hidden.
findings.mechanism: Sirat repeated in 1:6 and 1:7 supplies continuity of travel; its swallowing-through-the-throat image and penetrating sword image meet dallin's hiddenness and burial. Their contact makes invisibility a shared result of different operations, so a road that takes one onward need not be identical with a loss that cannot be followed.
findings.reader_payoff: The feared disappearance becomes more precise through comparison with directed passage.
findings.containment: Swallowing remains an explicit material analogy, the sword a sword, and burial an associated hiding operation; none translates the human route as a literal throat, weapon, or grave. The stallion does not provide attested disappearance. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

epistemic.reason: The source descriptors and contextual carriers are supplied; the transfer between them and the focus is an interpretive analogy with the primary meanings preserved.

findings.mechanism: Hamd supplies praise and thanks; al-alamin's knowing image supplies discernment; rabb's learned cultivation supplies sustained recognition; the praised person with many good traits makes recognition durable. Meeting the praise-formula family beside an'amta, these roles connect a benefit, its recognition, and its articulation.

findings.containment: The praise formula is a separate construction from Form IV bestowal and from the affirmative response. Its invocation is analogical, not a claim that an'amta is itself ni'ma or that the recipients are universally certified scholars. findings.title: Preserved Appearance with Failed Function
findings.claim: The eye-delight and eye-swelling images beneath favor and wrath can make the requested road sensitive to the gap between an intact appearance and the ability to see or continue.
findings.mechanism: Mustaqim's eye that remains intact without sight supplies the appearance/function distinction, its sheep-leg disease adds stalled gait, the guidance root's heavy weak person adds failed bodily responsiveness, and the worship root's stranded mount adds interrupted travel. The focus's gladdened eye and swollen eye then contrast different visual conditions without reducing them to mere location.
findings.reader_payoff: A path that looks available and a body that looks intact may still need enabling help to function.
findings.containment: The gladdened eye is a person-related blessing or good-wish construction, not a clinical restoration claim. Lid protrusion, swelling, blindness, leg disease, and strandedness remain different source images; bodily disability is not equated with spiritual fault. Counter-reading: the cited context can retain its ordinary senses without forming this material or relational analogy.

The favor root's attested bird-idiom of defeat and diminished collective force meets dallin's loss from a holder, completing the move from confrontation to dispersal and unrecovered loss.

The bird idiom remains construction-bound imagery; an'amta still bestows favor and does not state that the favored group was routed. findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: Favor and wrath are two symmetrical divine dispositions assigning opposite groups. Reconstructed after: Mercy is the persistent field of the route, while wrath is a bounded relational response marking resistance within that field.
findings.containment: The passive names recipients without naming an agent or proving their deliberate resistance. Mercy's repetition supports this framing as an inference; it establishes neither a ranking of attributes nor that wrath can have only one cause.  The packet supplies repeated tenderness, one passive wrath construction, and opposition; I infer that repetition and agency asymmetry bound wrath within mercy's field; a live alternative is that repetition has no governing force over the focus contrast.

findings.title: trajectories under reckoning
findings.claim: Ownership, a day horizon, and recompense can place the focus's road contrast within an eventual settlement, with cutting, compensation, retaliatory claim, and unlocated loss as a legal analogy for divergent outcomes.
findings.mechanism: Disposition, bounded time, and reckoning turn the focus partition into an accountable process. The road cuts among outcomes that eventually become settleable: benefaction carries forward, opposition incurs a retaliatory claim, and straying remains a loss until located and accounted for.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: The focus lists spiritually approved and disapproved populations. Reconstructed after: The focus can map trajectories by their status in an eventual settlement: advanced by favor, exposed to retaliatory claim, or still lost from account.
findings.containment: The ordinary day supplies a bounded image, not a claim that the Day of Recompense lasts a measured daylight interval. A trajectory lost from view is not outside divine knowledge or accountability. Compensation is a possible source-image fork, not an enacted transaction.  The packet supplies disposition, bounded time, reckoning, a cutting route, compensation, retaliation, and loss; I infer a settlement arrow from travel to accountable outcome; a live alternative is that the legal images only intensify contrast without forming a procedural sequence.

findings.title: assisted road underfoot
findings.claim: The contextual contact of humble worship, road-leveling, and requested aid with the favor root's foot-travel image can make the received road something enacted and maintained by assisted practice.
findings.mechanism: Humble service levels a way, walking places it underfoot, and requested assistance supplies the capacity to continue. The road is therefore partly enacted by repeated service rather than merely discovered as external geography.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: The road exists complete before the traveler and needs only to be pointed out. Reconstructed after: The road is received but also enacted underfoot: humble practice levels it, communal walking preserves it, and aid keeps the enactment possible.
findings.containment: The foot-travel branch is restricted to its attested walking-to-a-person and foot-use constructions. This is their material analogy, not a lexical translation of an'amta or a claim that human practice creates divine guidance from nothing.  The packet supplies worship, leveling, aid, foot travel, and road; I infer that assisted practice both traverses and makes the route; a live alternative is that worship only qualifies the petitioner and does not alter the road's material or social availability.

findings.title: guidance specified through people
findings.claim: The road repeated across 1:6 and 1:7 carries the guidance request into a specification by favored people and distinguishable failures, giving straightness a human diagnostic form.

The focus is thus not an independent taxonomy but the operational specification of what the requested straight road looks like in people and in failure.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: The focus independently divides people into three classes. Reconstructed after: The focus answers the guidance request by translating straightness into a favored human trajectory and two distinct diagnostic failures.
findings.containment: The continuation is grounded in repetition and the supplied focus analysis; the operational diagnostic is a qualified interpretation. No identities or moral histories of the two excluded groups are supplied.  The packet supplies gentle indication, repeated road, upright balance, favored condition, and deviation; I infer that 1:7 functions as a diagnostic answer to 1:6; a live alternative is that 1:7 merely appends historical examples without specifying the mechanism of straightness.

findings.title: guidance gift carried further
findings.claim: The guidance root's gracious gift meets bestowed benefit and furthering in the focus, allowing favored people to be pictured as relays through whom a received gift becomes available to later petitioners.
findings.mechanism: The gift-bearing branch of guidance resonates with active benefaction in the focus. Guidance can therefore be received as something sent through affection, while favored people are not only earlier users of the road but carriers through whom the gift reaches later petitioners.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: Favored people prove that guidance was given in the past. Reconstructed after: Favored people can be living relays through whom the guidance-gift is carried further to new petitioners.
findings.containment: Furthering does not lexically entail transmission between generations. The relay is the HFT's stated relational inference, held beside a gift directly from the divine addressee to each petitioner.  The packet supplies guidance-as-gift, transferred benefaction, furthering, and a recipient-defined road; I infer onward transmission through favored people; a live alternative is that gift imagery concerns only the divine-to-petitioner relation and does not make recipients into carriers.

findings.title: collectively maintained route
findings.claim: The prior straightness word's community, guardianship, and subsistence images can make the focus's favored plural a collective that helps keep the shared road supplied and available.
findings.mechanism: Community, custodial care, and material support turn straightness from an individual posture into maintained infrastructure. The favored collective bears, repairs, and supplies the route, so belonging to their road entails participation in its upkeep.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: Straightness is an individual traveler's correct alignment on a fixed road. Reconstructed after: Straightness is also a communal achievement: favored people keep the shared route standing, supplied, and available.
findings.containment: Collective upkeep is an analogy inferred from plural petition, plural recipients, care, and support. Mustaqim remains straightness; the group may also be read as individual exemplars without a joint maintenance role.  The packet supplies community, custodial care, support, road, and shared welfare; I infer that the group maintains the road as infrastructure; a live alternative is that the plural groups remain aggregates of individuals with no maintenance relation.

findings.title: growth corrected by measure
findings.claim: Attributed growth in rabb can meet favor's furthering and the straightness root's exactly weighted measure, making deviation the image of advance that has lost corrective proportion.
findings.mechanism: Increase and equal measure form a dynamic control system. Favor propels growth beyond the current state, while straightness continually corrects that growth toward proportion; deviation is not lack of motion but growth that has lost feedback.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: Straightness means preserving an unchanged mean and avoiding all departure from it. Reconstructed after: Straightness can be regulated growth: favor drives further development, while measure repeatedly corrects its direction.
findings.containment: The coin-weight branch keeps its specific equal-measure image; no financial coin is asserted in the focus. Feedback is an inference connecting stated images, not a lexical meaning of straightness or evidence that all growth requires a particular control theory.  The packet supplies increase, equal measure, furthering, and deviation; I infer a feedback arrow in which measure regulates growth; a live alternative is that increase and measure are unrelated branch images and straightness means only fixed conformity.

findings.title: provision as directed watercourse
findings.claim: The road's swallowing passage, favor's moist south wind, ghayr's watering and repair, wrath's rock, and straying's hiddenness can meet attributed rain and spring cues to picture provision as flow that reaches, is blocked, or is lost.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: The road is a dry surface carrying human travelers. Reconstructed after: Exploratorily, it can behave like a watercourse: favor replenishes and repairs along directed flow, hardness blocks it, and straying is flow that disappears without fructifying the marked terrain.
findings.containment: A watercourse analogy preserves road, bestowed favor, exclusion, wrath, and straying as their primary meanings. The name-to-rain and help-to-spring mappings are separately attributed; no independent lexicon gloss is supplied for them. Hidden water need not literally be wasted, and rock need not always block it. This is surprising because it coordinates branch-distant rain, spring, wind, swallowing, watering, and rock images across several roots. It remains anchored in the focus road, benefaction, exception, wrath, and disappearance branches, with context supplying actual water-system images. Downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for directed provision versus blocked or lost flow, never as a lexical replacement for the verse. The proposed image is exploratory; the contextual words can retain their ordinary roles without forming this analogy.

findings.title: protected hidden passage
findings.claim: The womb image of the opening mercy word can meet the road's interior passage, favor's softness, wrath's hard rock, and straying's disappearance to distinguish protected hidden formation from hiddenness without directed emergence.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: Successful travel should remain visible as continuous progress on an open road. Reconstructed after: Exploratorily, the favored route can include a hidden gestational interval in which disappearance is protected formation, while straying is hiddenness that does not emerge into directed life.
findings.containment: A gestational analogy, not a claim that sirat means birth canal, that divine mercy has bodily anatomy, or that every hidden interval ends in birth. Softness, obstruction, and loss remain analogical conditions of passage. This is surprising because a womb image is mapped onto a road and coordinated with swallowing passage, softness, compact obstruction, and hiddenness. It remains anchored through focus branches governing passage and its success or failure, while the context supplies the generative enclosure. Downstream prose should label it a gestational spatial analogy, not claim that the road noun means birth canal. The proposed image is exploratory; the contextual words can retain their ordinary roles without forming this analogy.

findings.title: watchful care and visual states
findings.claim: Attributed seeing and watchful care in the help word can meet favor's gladdened eye, wrath's eye-region swelling, straying's hiddenness, and the opening's attributed visible sign to differentiate how a traveler remains seen and able to see.
findings.reader_payoff: Reconstructed before: The three groups differ only by where they travel. Reconstructed after: Exploratorily, they also differ as visual relations: cared-for and gladdened sight, sight burdened by swelling, and disappearance beyond recoverable view.
findings.containment: This is explicitly a split-root visual activation. Help is not translated as eye, and an unresolved eye mapping has no invented branch gloss. Swelling does not entail blindness, eye delight does not clinically restore sight, and bodily impairment is not moral condemnation. This is surprising because the trigger comes from the non-dominant eye mapping of the help root and then recruits eye-related focus branches. It remains anchored in benefaction's gladdened eye, wrath's swollen eye, and straying's hiddenness, all attached to focus words. Downstream prose should explicitly call this a split-root visual activation and avoid translating help as eye. The proposed image is exploratory; the contextual words can retain their ordinary roles without forming this analogy.

findings.title: breaking test and standing

findings.containment: The demolition mapping is an attributed alternative to the canonical guidance root. The image describes ordeal and resilience, not a lexical equation of guidance with destruction or an injunction to break people or things. It remains anchored in the focus's cutting-road and hardened-wrath branches, while contextual standing supplies a coherent material counteraction. Downstream prose should render it as an ordeal-and-resilience image, not as the ordinary sense of guidance or road. The proposed image is exploratory; the contextual words can retain their ordinary roles without forming this analogy.

findings.title: The petitioner addresses the earlier giver
findings.claim: The 'You' who receives exclusive worship and help-seeking in 1:5 and the guidance imperative in 1:6 remains the explicitly named giver in an'amta. The request is made to the one whose benefaction has already reached others.
findings.mechanism: The second-person worship/help relation and imperative cross the ayah boundary into the perfect benefaction verb's second-person suffix. The plural 'us' asks for a road specified through 'them', placing present dependence in relation to an acknowledged prior act by the same addressee.
findings.reader_payoff: The favored group supplies a precedent for the petitioner's relationship with the giver; the wording itself connects request, gift, and earlier recipients.
findings.containment: The perfect bestowal is preserved, and the third-person recipients remain distinct from the first-person petitioners. Their favor's particular content, their names, and automatic admission of the petitioner are not specified.

epistemic.reason: The supplied context Arabic and the focus's aligned pronouns, government, and lexical forms support the relation directly; its reader-facing implication is stated with its boundary.

findings.title: The exclusions belong to the community's request
findings.claim: Because 1:7 completes the first-person-plural guidance request of 1:6, ghayr and the renewed la also delimit the path the speakers ask for themselves. The two excluded conditions remain within one petition.
findings.mechanism: The supplied focus analysis places genitive ghayr inside the repeated road chain and carries its exclusion across wa-la to the final active participle. The earlier 'guide us' keeps the same group of petitioners in view, so the negative boundary is a specification of their requested direction as well as a distinction among the named groups.
findings.reader_payoff: The speakers' dependence remains audible even while they name unwanted outcomes; the wording offers no grammatical assertion that they are already immune to them.
findings.containment: This does not identify the excluded populations or prescribe an attitude toward historical communities. The supplied alternative attachments of ghayr, to the people or to the path relation, remain open; both keep the boundary inside the petition.
